objective: Finish the named 1.6 spot, MHC, in-app sharing, responsive UI, accessibility, badge-menu, public report and appeal, and release-email changes while preserving all unrelated approved behavior.
userOutcome: The retained 100-mile Spot import remains available while a later re-scrape is deferred; Spot details and hover labels are compact and clear; MHC works for cruush+ from any distance; Spot and profile locations can be shared only inside cruush; responsive headers, badges, legal copy, colorblind mode, named hover states, public content-removal reports, and suspension appeals work; and the 1.6 email shows final rendered features.
audience: cruush members and the 1.6 release-email audience.
successCriteria: Preserve the retained public Spot import within 100 miles while deferring a new exhaustive scrape to a later session.
Use Leans men and Leans women where supported; remove gay spot, dyke spot, and dyke bar labels from the app.
Collect optional amenities during check-in and amenities, vibes, access instructions, and category when suggesting a spot.
Show top two aggregate vibes and amenities on spot details, with Pink Book access governed by check-in and Who's Here still publicly viewable.
Put the singular Spot category, back, and bug controls on one header line; keep the Spot name in page content; center the Spot hover label directly above its marker.
Render spot cluster counts without an icon and use the logo font for both people and spot cluster counts without changing map tiles or theme.
Signed-out bug reporters can supply email; signed-in reporters use their account email; email replies route between reporter and reports inbox.
Content-removal requests use a signed-out-capable form delivered to reports@cruush.app instead of opening an email to hello@cruush.app.

Suspension emails come from reports@cruush.app, state the specific suspension reason, and link directly to the matching signed-out age or general appeal form; signed-out forms require the email associated with the account.
A valid suspended-account sign-in opens a dedicated suspended screen with logout and the matching signed-out appeal form, without exposing account creation.
The badge heart preview does not scroll into the mobile top bar, and the desktop Badges tab renders its menu directly below the profile tabs.
MHC can be enabled by any cruush+ member regardless of travel distance while normal browsing remains limited to 50 miles around the actual location.
Spot and profile shares stay inside cruush and do not invoke external sharing.
Tablet headers have a centered maximum width with deployed-mobile icon sizing; Map Controls hover uses the deployed high-legibility state.
Mobile pages keep vertical scrolling but never show a side scrollbar.
The mobile Notifications header always shows Back, Notifications, Settings, and Bug on one line; bulk actions move below without hiding the title.

Auth legal copy uses the available width cleanly; researched Color-blind options cover common color-vision deficiency types across app and logo colors without altering member photos or map tiles; the landing tagline and Open Beta capsule hover glows read as neutral white above the warm video; and the logo hover glow uses a compact radius and the approved logo colors.
Landing layouts place About, Help, and Blog above the By continuing legal line without changing the approved glow targets.
Basic profiles can save up to 3 kinks; cruush+ profiles can select the full kink catalog without a product limit.
All members can choose current custom side badges; future badge packs remain deferred.
A local preview page groups every current badge icon by profile category, and the self-overlapping Gay badge icon is replaced without changing user-selected badge icons.
Mobile long-press reveals badge meanings while desktop hover remains; hanky labels do not overflow.
Larger Text scales every user-visible text style across the app while preserving usable layouts.

Basic members receive 1 Pulse per rolling day and cruush+ members receive 5; there is no sender cooldown, Pulse alerts remain optional, each recipient receives at most one Pulse alert every 4 hours, and the same sender cannot alert the same recipient more than once per day.
Group owners and admins can spend one of their own Pulses to alert members of that group; group Pulses obey the same recipient notification preferences and repeat limits as individual Pulses.
A successful Spot check-in creates one moderated public Feed post per member, Spot, and hourly check-in event while Pink Book posts remain separate and persistent.
Onboarding explains that Crowd Mode affects visibility only when enabled and includes the approved profile-photo rules.
Onboarding step 2 accepts an optional friend invite code and explains that invite benefits require the invited member to enable 2FA.

Onboarding places role and position before badges, shows the full uploaded-photo heart unit, and visibly defaults the left badge to role and the right badge to position when no custom badges are chosen.
Onboarding finishes with the oath and Code of Conduct acceptance.

After onboarding grants the free cruush+ day, first map entry shows its reward notification; tapping that notification opens the existing scratch-card interaction instead of opening the card automatically.
Spot clustering remains responsive with the expanded dataset.
Members can contribute Spot vibes, amenities, and access details without checking in or being near the Spot.
No public Spot source attribution names Sniffies; OpenStreetMap attribution remains where applicable.
Refresh the actual Spot, spot-cluster, badge-menu, MHC, and feed screenshots used by the 1.6 email and show the resulting email.
After implementation, add or update focused tests for the session rules and update the repository design-rules Markdown.
mustPreserve: Preserve approved custom map tiles, theme, people pins, Ghost Mode, Dark Room, Pulse, and unrelated map behavior.
Preserve existing published spots, check-ins, Pink Book posts, ratings, and unrelated 1.6 work.
Never display gay spot, dyke spot, or dyke bar as a public label.
Do not infer trans or nonbinary presence from profiles or scraped visitor data.
Harassment-only Stream results must publish with flagged moderator review, while mixed unsafe labels and non-harassment flags retain their existing enforcement.
Keep user-facing copy free of em dashes and spell cruush lowercase.
nonGoals: No map tile or theme changes, no reaction or feed-reply work, no crowd-mode changes, no new Spot scrape, no heart-halo or presence-indicator implementation, no phone verification or physical-device identity enforcement before 1.7, no public-group or party implementation before those features exist, no broad build, no push, and no deploy.
Do not import private residences, visitor identities, access codes, or covertly inferred identity attributes.
Do not redesign unrelated pages or add unrelated labels, taglines, controls, or filters.

assumptions.statement: The prior user-controlled Sniffies extraction may be reused if its full source cache can be recovered locally.
assumptions.impact: The complete public source set can be imported without a new competitor scrape.

assumptions.statement: Source-platform places can initially use Leans men, and independently sourced women-centered venues can use Leans women, while future crowd composition comes from cruush aggregate data.
assumptions.impact: Search has useful initial lean labels without gay or dyke labels or trans/nonbinary inference.

assumptions.statement: Public venue descriptions, non-sensitive access directions, and aggregate popular-time history are acceptable imports; private access details are not.
assumptions.impact: Spot details can be useful without exposing sensitive information.

nextVisibleMilestone: A local checkpoint commit plus refreshed rendered 1.6 email screenshots and email preview.
stopConditions: Stop the data-expansion slice if the full prior source cache cannot be recovered or if a source record is private or unsafe to publish.
Stop publication because push and deployment are not authorized by this task.
